In my years of life I’ve only found maybe half a dozen I can put up with. I usually avoid them - but because I enjoy them - I do try to find ways to use it. Because of these sensitivities I try not to “blame” the product, unless it burns - then I have to question what all is in there. In the end, I do like this Atlas Semi Matte Texture Putty 2.4 Ounce is a Medium Shine for how it works and how it looks. But for sensitive guys, you need to be aware, this putty has a strong scent - in my case at least, too strong. I won’t be able to keep using it.

I've been using this just before showering in the morning, and then using the shower to rinse it off--and here's the unexpected side effect: my miserable early spring sinuses have improved! I think it's the herbs in the product coupled with the steam from the shower, but my whole sinus area feels SO much more open. Hooray!

I'm thrilled with this product. My skin feels awake and energized, and the products I use daily--serums, moisturizer, and BB cream--just sink right in after use. "Meh". I've never used 'beard oil' before, so just for the helluvit decided to give some a try, and grabbed the trial pack (original scent).

This is pretty much just greasy. Feels and smells mostly like you're just rubbing Vaseline on your beard, though a bit lighter.

The package:
The presentation is actually really nice. Nice little velvet bag with a string, the balm/oil, and even a guitar pick.

The result:
Yes, my beard felt a *little* softer, and was a *little* less frazzled looking, though not much more than if I just comb it after a shower. I'm not really sure why I'm seeing so many RAVE reviews; it's not *that* great. I can take it or leave it.

text:
Rich lotion with an ingredient that I'm not a fan of.. It's me again. That Irish girl with the picky skin :)
This time we are trying Clia Natural Facial Moisturizer.
I like when a product has an easy to read ingredients panel, either on their product, or the accompanying box. If not, at least have on their product page a complete list of ingredients so I know what's in it, so I can make an informed decision if this is a product for me and my sensitive skin.
The box I received this product in was a simple, plain cardboard box.
The writing on the label is miniscule at best.
I blew up the attached images so I could read what it actually said. One of the first 5 ingredients is Palm Oil. I'm not a fan of Palm Oil for environmental reasons. The growth and harvest of palm oil is not kind to our planet. That's my personal feelings on the matter.

The cream itself is very rich and smooth without a chemical smell, more like your typical face cream.
I did the back of my hand test first to check for a reaction. There was none, so the next morning I applied the cream to one half of my face for the "face" test.
This cream is VERY rich. Just lightly tap your fingers on the open jar, and you'll get just the right amount. A little goes a long way.
I applied it to my forehead, cheek and neck. It absorbed fairly quickly with no greasy residue.
DId it pass the no breakout, no hives test? Yes it did, and my skin felt softer throughout the day without drying out or leaving any dry patches.
Overall, it's a good, luxurious feeling lotion, but with that Palm Oil in there, i'm not 100% on board, so, I'm really at 3.75 stars on this product
Disclosure: I received this product at a discount for my honest review.

5.) This stuff is widely discounted and it seemed like a low risk option to learn about Vetiver and answer some of my questions.

So how does it smell? Great! I loved it from the first moment of the first spray through the dry down right up until it disappeared on my skin.

Reviewers use words like "dark, brooding, mysterious, and serious" to describe this. I don't get any of that. It just smells good. It makes me happy. No, it's not a light citrus smell for summer days. It's a heavier, richer smell that's probably better for an evening out.

Personally I find this a lot like the Dolce & Gabbana The One EDP I also bought. The smell is totally different but with both these fragrances.........
1.) I just liked the smell from the first moment.
2.) The concentration is Eau De Parfum for both.
3.) The longevity, projection, and sillage seems similar.

And speaking of performance, this is NOT "beast mode" stuff. It's more subtle. And as a newcomer I'm learning that can be a good thing or a bad thing depending on the circumstances when you're wearing it. But for the most part, subtle is safer and understated is the classier way to go. So for both the D&G The One EDP and this Encre Noir A L'Extreme these impress me as grown up fragrances that come off as sophisticated scents for grown men who wear suits for a living. text:
Poor Overall Performance and Longevity. I bought this in July and began using it in early September. It seemed like it would be easy to use, as well as clean and maintain. The extra features included a beard trimmer, a nose-hair trimmer, and a face brush. There was also a charging cord but no actual charger.

I ended up using this every day for about 100 days before the lid broke for the cutter housing. It broke right where you would expect at the hinge after normal opening and closing for cleaning per the instructions. For what I paid for the shaver, it didn't seem worth it to try and find a replacement cutter housing.

The shave itself is by far the worst I've ever gotten from an electric shaver. I did use it consecutively for more than several weeks to allow my face to adjust. This wasn't the issue as my face was already used to using electric shavers and I had no adjustment period issues with my face. The issue was that the cutters were just plain dull and ineffective. Even with three heads I would say I spent at least twice as long shaving with this shaver as compared to my last one. Though it has three cutting heads, I would sometimes have to make a half a dozen passes over the same area before the stubble was cut flush with my skin.

The shaver seemed to use a lot of charge for a single shave. Enough of a charge that it typically took 4+ hours to fully recharge after a single shave. I'm not sure if it was the battery or the charging cord but the charger was actually the same one I used with the previous shaver with much better results.

The nose hair trimmer worked well. I never used the beard trimmer or facial brush.

After cheaping out on this unit, I ended up buying a Panasonic Arc4 for 3 times more than what I spent for this one but so far it is absolutely worth the extra money. Do yourself a favor and don't cheap out and buy this like I did.

text:
Good for what you pay for. I like to fashion myself as sort of a cologne connoisseur…….a man’s man who just really likes to smell good all the time. I began wearing cologne shortly after I started my first job in high school, and ever since then I have been enamored with finding great smelling colognes. When I saw this cologne, and I read what it was inspired by, I felt that it was almost a must have for me.

The first and most obvious reason most of us on here purchased this cologne is because it is inspired by Ralph Lauren Polo Red; and since that cologne is fairly pricey, undoubtedly most of us felt they were going to get a sweet deal. Now, you may ask what is the difference between this and the legitimate cologne that you would pay 60$ or more for?

The first thing to know is that this cologne does not smell exactly like Polo Red at all. In fact, it is very loosely inspired by the actual scent. I challenge anyone to buy and smell the original cologne, then buy and smell this and tell me it’s exactly the same thing. Sorry folks, this just isn’t the same smell. It does, however, share similarities with the Polo Red…..which makes it enticing, but it just is not the same thing.

The main issue that I have with this cologne is that it simply does not last more than an hour at best. I now understand why you get a 3.0-ounce bottle for 15$, and that is because you are constantly reapplying it to keep the smell fresh. With a normal (and quality) cologne I can go pretty much the extent of my eight-hour shift at work and still smell relatively fresh, but this cologne honestly started fading at about 20-30 minutes after application.

In the end this may not bother folks who just want something cheap to make them smell good for a little while. Heck, even I like the way it smells at first. The problem for those of us who fashion ourselves fragrance snobs is that the scent just fades away too quickly.

I think it is a great buy and you will have perfumed oil forever if you use wisely and buy bigger bottles of the fragrances you love. I’m happy with this purchase.

Smells great! If it only lasted beyond a few hours..... I consider myself to be a cologne snob. I like good cologne and I am not afraid to spend good money for it.

So, when I see something like Intense Energy available for about a quarter less in price than what most good colognes cost, I become a bit suspicious as to its shortcomings.

This fragrance is inspired by Polo Red Cologne. I am familiar with Polo (I used to wear it in the 80s), and the aroma does have hints of that brand's scent. It smells pretty good. It's not overpowering.

The problem is, it just doesn't last. I put on a hefty dose of 4 sprays across my neck and clothing. The scent had faded within an hour or two. By the end of an 8 hour workday, I couldn't even smell the scent on my clothing, or when I rubbed my finger across my neck.

Obviously, this is a cologne geared more towards affordability than lasting scent. If you don't mind carrying it with you all day and re-applying it when needed, it won't be a bad purchase decision.

text:
Great Product that Works. Face Moisturizers, and cosmetics in general, are typically not available or made with men in mind, so it is refreshing to find a beauty-type product and product line that caters to the male of the species.

Gentlehomme is certainly on to something pleasantly surprising, with a face moisturizer that contains many of the ingredients you might find in higher end products for women, such as collagen, oils, Vitamin E (tocopherol), butters, and stem cells. The ingredient list is rather exhaustive, with probably more than you need, but I have to appreciate a product that is well thought out. In terms of just the 'butters' and 'oils', the face moisturizer includes Cocoa Seed Butter, Coconut Oil, Avocado Oil, Bitter Orange Flower Oil, and Jojoba Seed Oil.

Unlike a few other reviews I've read of this product, I did not find the product to be greasy at all. It absorbed rather quickly into the skin, leaving it soft and supple, with a slight glow, without being shiny. It does have a thick, white, whipped consistency to it, similar to other facial creams out there, such as Noxzema. Also being four ounces, rather than two ounces, which is more standard for facial creams, makes this a pretty good value, overall.

Also unlike other comments that I've read, I did not find the Neroli scent overpowering or unlikeable at all. With that said, however, I found the smell to be very faint and more non-descript than of Neroli (Bitter Orange). The fragrance is very light--not necessarily masculine as one might expect, but almost indistinguishable from most other products out there--not offensive but not remarkable. My nose is rather sensitive to scents and I would have difficulty picking this one out in a crowd.

I like that I didn't have any negative reaction(s) to the product--no burning or stinging, rash or inflammation, and the moisturizer held up all day and all night without any discomfort or facial skin drying.

Review of the product
The comb comes with a black pull string pouch and is packed into a zippered plastic case. The comb is made of green sandal wood and is two sided. The teeth are spaced at about 1/32 inch and the teeth on both sides are spaced the same. When you place the comb near the nose it has a wonderful, fragrant sandalwood scent.

This comb has a medium brown finish with greenish streaks in the wood. It is very attractive in appearance. It is 3 and 13/16 inches long from end to end, 2 and 5/16 inches wide and approximately 3/8 inches thick at the center of the handle which tapers to pointed teeth on each side.

The comb is sturdy and feels good in the hand. Both sides taper to a nice smooth finish with a well-rounded, but not sharp point. “HAWATOUR” is etched into the wood. This comb weighs 1.1 ounces on the food scale.

Experience using the product
My daily routine is to massage a quality beard balm followed by quality beard oil into the beard and skin. I then brush my beard with a boar bristle brush and comb my beard for a couple of minutes. I comb periodically through the day and generally do the Balm/oil massage in the morning and again after a bath or shower in the evening. All pimples, chaffing, beardruff, itching and irritation have gone away since performing this routine.

This comb gives a therapeutic feeling and the teeth do not scrape the skin like plastic combs do. I purchased this comb for my son who also wears a thick beard. He does not and probably will not carry this comb in his pocket for risk of losing or breaking it.

For When You Want to Wash Your Face More Than Once. UPDATE: I've changed this review from 2 stars to 1 star, because the seller has repeatedly contacted me, most recently asking me outright to delete the review in exchange for a refund. The language was as follows: "Could you please forgive me and help me delete the review? If you can, I want to refund ($28) to you to express my gratitude. Please accept my little wish.Thank you."

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
First, the good: I enjoy the smell of this product. And I'll probably use the whole stick just because it smells nice, and provides a light tingling sensation. Apart from that, I've noticed no difference in moisture (blackhead reduction, or any of the other laundry list of things it claims to cure).

I got a decent laugh out of my first use, quickly realizing you can't simply roll this onto your face for complete coverage. You have to get this on your fingers to cover the contours of the nose, for example. The description of the product mentions "Blackhead Removal Strips", but those were nowhere to be found in what I received. Once this dries, I simply wash it off of my face, and see/feel exactly what I did when I initially washed my face the first time. Lastly, it's a bit overpriced as far as facial masks go.

So look, I like the soothing sensation of masks as much as the next person. Therefore please understand that I far from hate this product. I simply don't think it's providing much value. Even the satisfaction of a peel-able mask is absent here. But if you really want to pay to smell some tingling green tea drying on your face, then this will get you there. I just wouldn't expect much else from it. The laughably fake "before and after" shots should tell you plenty about the true efficacy of this product.

text:
Very good clone, moderate longevity. Grand Parfums Versace Eros opens with a strong projection of citrus, fruity, sweet, musky and spicy notes. The opening is very fresh, sharp, bright, inviting, unique, and delectable. The green apple, mint, ambroxan, and lemon are the most prominent opening notes. The lemon is the fresh and bright opening note, astringent, sour, and vibrant; the green apple is by its side, delectable, sweet, sour, crispy, and acidic. The mint rounds up the opening with its cooling green and slightly spicy note. The ambroxan is also noticeable musky, lemony, and ambery note that works well, improving the fragrance's projection. As the fragrance moves towards its dry down, the tonka bean and vanilla add a sweet and aromatic touch without making the fragrance overly sweet or taking the focus away from the mint, green apple, and lemon. The vetiver, oakmoss, and cedar are part of the support notes; they combine their notes to create a fresh green and woody accord but remain in the back of the fragrance. The fragrance is linear, all notes come up as soon as the fragrance is applied and continue into the dry down. Once Grand Parfums Versace Eros has reached its full dry down, it can be summarized as a strong projection, spicy mint, fruity green apple, musky ambroxan, mildly sweet vanilla, tonka, and woody cedar fragrance. The fragrance feels casual, comforting, delectable, energizing, exquisite, fresh, fruity, green, high-quality, inviting, masculine, modern, musky, nicely-blended, playful, refreshing, rich, sharp, seductive, sour, sparkly, special, sweet, unique, versatile, wild, woody, and very pleasant.

text:
Works wonders for taming frizz. Smells like clove though, not citrus.. Ladies and gentlemen, let me appeal to the ladies on the great results that beard oil can have on your hair. If you have wavy, frizzy, unmanageable hair (as I do), this could really help! I had been using argan oil and other oil blends to tame my wild hair, and when I read the ingredients in my roommate's beard oil and saw how similar they were, I wanted to give it a try. I first bought the Tea Tree blend by Beardsmen Spirit, since I'm a big fan of the benefits of tea tree oil, and I liked it so much that I wanted to try out this Rousing Citrus blend.

As far as ingredients go, the Rousing Citrus blend has Jojoba seed oil, sweet almond oil, grape seed oil, glycerin, grapefruit peel oil, lemon fruit oil, blood orange essential oil, clove flower oil, and vanilla plantifolia fruit essential oil. I compared this to the ingredients in the Tea Tree blend, which are Jojoba seed oil, sweet almond oil, grape seed oil, glycerin, peppermint essential oil, tea tree leaf essential oil, and vanilla plantifolia fruit essential oil. Not too big of a difference except for the obvious different essential oils. This oil has about the same thick consistency, and a little bit goes a long way! It takes about 5-6 drops of the oil to tame the frizz in my hair that's about 4 inches down past my shoulders.

One con for me though: this oil does not really have a citrus smell. I smell clove over everything else, and while this isn't a bad thing, I was really hoping for those lemon and blood orange essential oils to be prominent. So a more appropriate name for this would be "Rousing Clove".

text:
Unique. . .Maybe Too Unique. This is a really neat razor that has one possible issue, which I'll get to later.

The handle is big and heavy, and its unusual shape is very stylish. It gives a nice shave, too. If you have a small face or tight features, the large head might be a bit tricky to use in some areas, but that hasn't been a major issue. I usually use an old-school double-edge razor, not a flexing cartridge razor, so the fixed head angle isn't an issue for me. If you're used to a razor with a movable head, this one might take some getting used to.

The included shaving foam smells good and works well. You don't get a lot, but you don't have to use a large amount of it.

The "stand" is just a heavy metal cylinder with a round hole in the top and a pad on the bottom. The hole is wider than the razor handle, and just deep enough that the razor doesn't topple out. It's kind of weird, like the stand was designed for something else, but I guess it works.

I'm not sure why they call this package a "travelling razor kit." It comes in a large gift box, and doesn't include any sort of travel case or bag. Plus, it's the biggest, heaviest razor I've ever seen (aside from folding straight razors). I wouldn't even think of taking this thing on a trip.

Despite all the good things about this razor, there's one major red flag: At the moment, replacement blades aren't listed on Amazon or on the Suprent website. The package includes two cartridges and a card to get a third for free, but there's no guarantee that more will be available when you need 'em. While the included cartridges are definitely good for several shaves apiece, if that's all you get, you'll soon be left with a very expensive paperweight. I rated the product based on my use of it, but recommend that you verify the availability of replacement cartridges before buying.

text:
Leaves You Feeling Silky Smooth. Like another reviewer, this was not an item I would have selected myself. I received it as a gift from a friend and was hesitant to use it out of fear that it would have an overpowering floral smell due to the lavender. However, the bar ended up being a pleasant surprise, and I will likely buy it again.

Since I don't like too many bubbles in my bath and, more importantly, like stretching my Lush products as much as possible due to the cost, I cut the bar into fourths. I found it to be a lot harder to cut than most Lush products, so if you're going to cut it, use a really strong knife and be ready for it to blow apart a bit as you slice through. (It's pretty crumbly.)

What I like about this bar is that, even though it's not very bubbly -- even as someone who cuts bars, I usually get more from others than this one -- it leaves a wonderful silky feeling on your body. I love that, even in the water, I can feel it on my legs, and not in an annoying greasy way at all. It's so relaxing! I usually put cocoa butter on my legs after shaving, and I don't need to do anything after using this bar. It has some sort of wonderful lotion quality about it that I adore. More than the scent or bubbles, that is the reason I will purchase it for myself in the future.

The only objection I have is that it seems to melt a bit more than other bubble bars. I've kept it in a sealed container in a cool area, but it just doesn't keep well. If you're going to cut it, be sure to use the other pieces within a couple weeks at the most. And, like all bubble bars, don't get it wet unless you're going to use it right away, because even the tiniest bit of moisture gets it going.

text:
Another MUST TRY from Etude House!. This is a review for all three of the moisturizers.

Green Tea - This mask is for people who deal with excess sebum. That being said, I use this one the most. Not only does my skin feel hydrated instead of greasy in the morning, but after the third use I noticed less breakouts around my chin and jawline (I have hormonal acne and horribly sensitive skin).
Black Tea : This mask improves elasticity of the skin. I haven't used this long enough to notice a huge difference, but my skin does feel plump when I wake up, and my mom has had the same result!
Strawberry - Like most strawberry skin care products, this one is for people who deal with dry skin. I won't need to use this until the cold seasons arrive, but my mom needs heavy moisturizing products year-round. Her skin has definitely been looking more hydrated and brighter!

Instructions and ingredients are provided on the boxes, both in Korean and English.

I only have two small complaints about the products:
1. There's a very noticeable amount of fragrance. They all smell great, but it's a bit strong. Thankfully, the smell does fade after the moisturizer is massaged into the skin. My face normally can't tolerate products with so much fragrance, but so far all has gone well.
2. The packaging. Yes, it is adorable, but I'd prefer the spoon be able to stay in the cup. You use the spoon to scoop out the tapioca pearls and smash them up in your palm. It's a long spoon, and it pulls out a lot of moisturizer with it. With this product a little goes a long way (which makes it a total steal at it's current price), so I scrape off a lot of excess.

Like I said, those are small complaints, so this product is very much worth trying out. So long as Etude House keeps making it I'll keep buying it.

As any soap user knows, once the bar is used down to a certain size, it's ready to be replaced. And since these pieces are already so small, it's not long before you reach the replacement decision point, but x 3, as opposed to x 1 for a normal sized bar of soap. So for a very high price for what's a normal sized bar of soap cut up three ways, you'll be going through these bars fast, possibly wasting more, and needing to buy more sooner -- not eco-friendly!

The package is meant to give the impression of being earthy and eco-friendly. It's in a high-quality cardboard box (and not the recycled cardboard type), and the soap is surrounded with some shredded newspaper to give the impression of recycling/repurposing. text:
French Soap: It will Forever Change Your Definition of the Word "Soap". About twenty years ago, I made my first trip to France. Since we were there for a few weeks, I had to purchase some bar soap, and picked up, at random, some Provencal soap at our local supermarket (soap is soap, right? who cares what brand it is?).

When I first used it, the shock I experienced was something that made me realize that the soap I had been using all my life wasn't really "soap," at all, but was rather a chemical concoction. Of course, it works. It's just that when I tried my first bar of milled soap from the Provence in France I immediately could see all the differences: the silky smooth lather, the smell that was real, not chemical; the cleaning power; the feeling after drying off. An absolutely different experience.

Since that time, my wife and I regularly bring back as much real Provencal soap as we can when we visit France. It's actually not that expensive in France, at least for the standard brands. But the difficulty is the weight: putting all this soap in your suitcase pushes against airline luggage weight limits, and it has become a standard challenge we deal with each trip. But that how much we like this REAL soap.

Now, here's the thing. You can go to shops in the United States, and find soaps that say "Made in France," and so you just believe it. Do a little digging, however, and you'll find that there are companies that market soap in the US with the words "Made in France" emboldened across the front are not actually selling something made in France: it's that they are getting one small component of their blend from France, and then manufacture it here very much like any other US soap is made. I feel this is fraudulent, yet it is such an arcance subject that no one cares to look into it. But anyone who has tried the real thing knows the difference.

text:
S&S Hydrate and Clubman Pinaud Review. This review compares the Clubman "Pinaud 2-in-1" and Stubble & Stache "Hydrate" face/beard moisturizers, so I'm posting this same review for both products.

I have a short beard and have tried many brands and product types to manage the itchy skin and stiff hair. Over the years I experimented and decided that I did not like beard oils (for skin under beard) nor beard balms (conditions beard). So, I wanted to try something else - and discovered "beard friendly" leave-in facial creams. These are not wash-out conditioners, but are used after cleaning/shaving and left on your skin and in your beard. I only found these two products, so maybe this is a new product type?

Bottom line: Clubman is more like a traditional facial moisturizer that isn't bad for your beard, whereas S&S is a beard conditioner that isn't bad for your skin. I prefer S&S, but is much more expensive.

-- review --

Feel: The Clubman's thickness is more like a traditional facial moisturizer and spreads easily over the skin. S&S is thicker that the average facial cream. I applied the Clubman on the face/nose first, and then worked down to the neck, finishing with the beard, but with the S&S I started on the beard and worked out. Different, but both are workable.

Scent: The Clubman has a sharp floral scent, and other reviews say this scent is the same across the Clubman products. The S&S has a subtle metallic scent. I prefer the S&S's scent compared to Clubman's, but that depends on the person (and who you let close to you).

"Sparingly", to me, is a small (i.e. size of a dime - or less) amount applied with damp/wet hands. The product delivers a slick and fragrant after shaving experience that I highly recommend.

Many things can go wrong in a shave (i.e. quality of cream, sharpness of blade, aggressiveness of razor, etc.) but the last step of the shave, the closing act, is the application of the balm which will tell you all you need to know and remember about your shave before you tackle the rest of the day.
I've learned that Castle Forbes aftershave balm delivers time and again. No pain or burn. No sticky slather with overwhelming or lingering scent. Just quality and value - well worth the price and experience - you'll see.

I'm a great fan of the Castle Forbes shaving cream - but - while I like the strong lime scent upon application, and that it does not linger more than a few minutes after application, I can't justify the price vs. value on this one. text:
Fantastic, true clay Pomade!. This is by far the best pomade that I have ever used, and I have tried a lot. I have very thick hair that needs a lot of hold to stay manageable all day without drooping. I prefer a matte finish without a sweet perfume or artificial scent; and I swear by products with actual clay (bentonite) as a primary component, with less artificial chemicals.

I was a little concerned that the Coal Mine Clay would not have enough hold, given it is advertised as medium hold, but that is an understatement...this has much more hold than other products that claim high hold. This is a thick, water-based, clay that becomes less viscous when rubbed between your hands to make it easy to apply. It feels bit dry when you apply it, and you can feel it 'grab' your hair. It is easy to style, and sets up rapidly, without becoming stiff - it remains pliable, but keeps your hair supported. The clay is also good for your hair, and the pomade also contains hemp oil, which gives it a present aroma and is also healthy for the hair and scalp.

It has an understated, earthy scent, with a bit of hemp and woody aroma. I definitely don't get the dish soap suggested in another review. My wife really likes the scent - and says it is 'manly'.

I used to use Boogies Casual Hair Clay from Dollar Shave Club, which is a good clay based pomade, but ordering was a pain, and it was a bit expensive. I have subsequently tried about two dozen other pomades, particularly those advertised as clays and matte finish. Very few have actual clay, and even if they do then it is not a major ingredient. Many end up being more waxy or greasy, with less hold, and too much perfume.

Give this a try, and you'll be hooked.

text:
Versache meets the "modern" market.... As the product is marketed for, it should only be used for casual affairs seeing as how while it is complex enough for formal affairs, it smells too much like something you'd wear with jeans as opposed to a suit and tie.

As previously mentioned this product is slightly complex featuring sharp characteristics that designer brands typically have, as opposed to more mellow notes commonly thought to be the key success behind marketing casual-use perfumes. In that regard I think Versache lives up to its name with this product: they manage to deliver something highly creative, if not long lasting.

text:
Surprisingly good stuff.. Having long given up finding appropriate product for my beard, I bought a tin of Beard Balm Leave-in Conditioner (BBLIC) by Premium Nature on a lark. (Impulse shopping. Darn you, Amazon lightning deals!) Nonetheless, I've applied BBLIC every two or three days for a couple of weeks -- not long enough to render a final opinion but long enough to assess the primary attributes and contrast this product with others that I've tried.

BBLIC is effectively unscented. The initial light orange-citrus scent quickly dissipates. BBLIC is hydrophobic. Water beads on my fingers after I use them to apply the product. It's easily removed from fingers with a little soap. BBLIC is a conditioner. It softens and helps calm those wild hairs. It supports "natural" styling. However, it won't hold "architectural" styling.

While I'm pleased with what BBLIC does do, I'm also pleased with what it doesn't do. In contrast with some other products that I've tried, these things that have not (yet) happened. BBLIC has not made my face or beard feel greasy. BBLIC has not transferred onto my hands nor smudged onto my glasses. BBLIC has not irritated my skin or pores. BBLIC has not caused a dermatophyte bloom.

I remain undecided if and how BBLIC would fit into my grooming routine long term. So far, it is inoffensive and has some nice effects. That's a great start.

text:
CK Free... Definitely in my Top 10..!!. Guys, CK Free is one of my top fragrances... It is almost intoxicating..!! I only wish it lasted longer...

Out of the bottle, Free offers that clean fresh smell with a blend of citrus, juniper, woodsy, and (call me crazy) leather. It is truly a pleasant scent that will work in all seasons and for any occasion. The only downside is the longevity - lasting only about 4 hours (at most). The projection/sillage is great early on and then fades after the first hour. Our noses are all different - in my opinion, Free differs from the other CK fragrances I own (probably 5 others) in that it is not as "sweet", or I detect less floral notes.

Early on, Free has potential "Wow Factor". I have not received compliments, but Sweetie gives two thumbs up. The interesting thing here, she is not a huge fan of the "clean" and "fresh" scents - she prefers the "musk" or "spice" scents. To reiterate, it has potential..!!

In addition to the fragrance/scent, the bottle is one of my favorites. Other than the CK logo, the bottle is totally clear showing the clarity of the fragrance. It may be my favorite bottle in my collection. Additionally, the packaging is above average.

All things considered, I give CK Free 4.2 stars out of 5 stars. The scent is one of my favorites. If the longevity were better, Free would clearly be in my Top 5. It is a long way to the top if you want to rock-n-roll.

text:
Decent Petroleum-free pomade (Not that heavy of a hold though). I bought this as an alternative to Lockhart's Heavy. My biggest consideration was that O'Douds is free from petrolatum, with Lockhart's there was noticeable flaking and overall unhealthy feeling to my scalp. That being said, Lockhart's holds like crazy, the strongest I've ever used. If Lockhart's is a 10/10 then O'Douds is more like a 7.5-8/10.

The smell of the pomade is VERY strong, I hope you and people around you like the smell of tea tree oil. Because it's going to follow you for days, and get on anything your head touches. Lockhart's is similar, but with Lockhart's the smell fades after a day and only reappears when you reapply. O'Douds scent will follow you everywhere as long as a trace remains. That being said, I don't like the smell of Lockhart's. It has a much more, i dunno, tar like smell to me. Some people say the Lockhart's is vanilla and tobacco, but its more like a heavy smokers old clothing. So +1 to O'Douds for a better smell, but -1 to O'Douds for the intensity and permanence of the scent.

I would compare O'Douds, in terms of hold characteristics to something like Murray's. That is, Lockhart's is so strong it can straighten wavy hair, whereas O'Douds will straighten a bit but will tend to accentuate the waviness. Not my preference. O'Douds has a ton of shine where Lockhart's is quite matte. The O'Douds also stays "wetter" then the Lockhart's, good if you like to re-comb but bad if you want your hair to stay the way you combed it all day (like me).

Overall: I do like the O'Douds. I think they did a great job given the lack of petrolatum. Conversely I'll probably be using a mix of Lockhart's heavy (hold characteristics I like) and O'Douds (no petrolatum, better scent)

text:
Great oil, good scent.. I have tried a couple of other Beardsmen Spirit products, and I have absolutely loved them. So, I figured, why not give this one a try as well? Even though I was a little skeptical of the scent, I went ahead and did it. I won't say I wasn't pleased with the results, but it certainly wasn't my favorite.

First off, the product works amazingly well. I love what it does with my beard. I have generally rather scratchy and coarse beard hair, and this beard oil has done a remarkable job of softening up my beard. My wife has been greatly appreciative of the difference, and I am greatly appreciative of her appreciation...if that makes sense.

Now, as for the scent. I was less than crazy about it. The combination of mint and tea tree is pleasant enough, to be sure, but the end result is a very sweet smell. Again, there is nothing bad about it, I just prefer more of a "woodsy" scent, and this isn't it. My wife likes it, which, again, I like. But, I'm the one wearing it, and the Tea Tree scent just isn't for me. In all honesty, I will definitely keep it around, but I will probably just use it during the Christmas season, as a fun little holiday thing.

So, to sum up, if you are looking for a sweet, minty, scent, and an amazing beard oil, you should buy this product. You won't be disappointed by the result.

text:
Strange product. I may have gotten this because of the hype in the description. I mean, "SPICE UP ANY ROOM WITH A SIGNATURE FRAGRANCE THAT WILL NEVER GO AWAY," is an awesome tagline, if not a little chilling. I mean, never?!? It also makes your stinky clothes fresh and can take away dandruff and clean your hair. Yes, it's a little unbelievable, but if even half that is true...

So I got this small bottle to try. It smells like baby powder. Very strong, concentrated baby powder. It may indeed "never go away." But some people really like the smell of baby powder, and, even though I never used baby powder on my babies, it still brings back a nostalgia. It's pleasant. I do not know if baby powder will "spice" up a room, but it might be more pleasant that what is stinking up the place, and this will supersede many odors. I'm skeptical of the other claims as well. text:
Stick with non-bulk purchases for this product...it seems these are so cheap for a reason. I am a fan of this lip balm...the low-profile case fits in a pocket quite well and is much handier than other brands. Being on a bike, you don't want a lot of bulky things to carry, so this slim balm is just great. Being able to get this many for this cheap was just great...almost 'too good to be true'.

However...t tried a few different ones from different parts of the box I received and each one has a terrible smell and worse taste (I know it isn't edible, but you do occasionally get a little in your mouth). You can detect a hint of the mint/wax scent I am used to from this product, but there is an overwhelming odor of cardboard soaked in vomit. It's awful. The entire box is unusable. If you think odor isn't important, just remember that your lips tend to be a bit close to your nose...you smell it CONSTANTLY. I'm guessing these were all so cheap because they were stored improperly or in a place they were able to absorb odor from something quite foul. I am VERY disappointed and will never buy this in bulk again...turns out it really was too good to be true.

This isn't Lava Soap, Fast Orange, or some other heavy duty hand cleaner. It's an all natural, GREAT smelling bar of soap. If you need something stronger, better buy IT first.
I've seen some reviewers complain about how long it lasts, claiming only 3 days. The photo I posted is after 30 days of use. Yes, 1 month. Now, I'm not a huge guy. 5'6", 150 lbs, average build. Most days I shower twice a day, once before work and once after I work out or get filthy working on a project. I keep the soap in a draining soap dish so it isn't soaking in a bowl of water. I also use it as shaving cream, as I shave my head and face while in the shower. So I don't know what happened to reduce the bar to a lump of goo in only 3 days.
If you keep it in a soap dish that fills with water and doesn't drain, your soap won't last as long. If you are 6'9", 350 lbs, your soap won't last as long. if you are eating it, it won't last as long. if you are allergic to something in the soap, it's not the soap's fault.
I am about to try the next flavor in the pack, so I'll update my review then.
Meanwhile, I love this stuff and fully recommend it! Worth the price (which admittedly could be a little less.)

text:
Why you (and I) need a beard brush. Review from husband:

Why would you need a beard brush? I'm glad that you asked! I spent years with facial hair and never gave it a thought. A quick trim from time-to-time, and I thought that I was good. It's a simple life, and it's good, but the health of your beard can reflect the health of your entire body. A beard brush does several things: it exfoliates the skin underneath the beard, helping to prevent ingrown hairs and dryness. It helps to evenly distribute naturally occurring oils in the hair, and lastly, it smooths the hairs of your beard, "filling in" thinner spots on the face and leaves you with a smooth, uniform look. This oval-shaped brush fits well in the hand, and has a feeling of quality. The bristles are stiff, but that is actually a good thing, as it assists in the performance listed above. If you have sensitive skin or have never used a brush on your face before, use a light touch. I like to brush out my beard before bed, and anytime I need to look good.

The balm has a light scent that is pleasant, but isn't overly masculine. It has a thick, waxy consistency out of the jar, and can take a bit of work to melt in the hands. Once applied to the beard however, it moisturizes nicely, and leaves no oily residue. Facial hair can get brittle and have split ends, and a high quality conditioner/balm like this one is worth buying. Make the investment and take the time to put your best face forward.

Good but Nothing Overly Impressive. I am writing this review after having used this lotion for a good week or two. Some things that I can't judge yet are the scars and discoloration. I do not have extreme acne scars or discoloration so I have a feeling that any change I can review on will have to wait. At the moment I do not see any drastic changes so I can't give it 5 stars in good conscious.

The only con that I have so far is the smell. It isn't overly bad per say so it isn't unusable. The scent is actually pretty nice when you first apply it. A soft lavander/floral scent that I wish would stick. After a good second after applying it the scent actually changes into something hard to describe besides off putting.

I give it three stars at the moment because of this and because it hasn't been anything special. It doesn't make my face silky smooth or bring out anything more than spectacular. text:
The other reviews are unfair... I'm happy this product is back. I felt compelled to write this review because of all the other bad reviews, which I think are very unfair. And I don't want this product that I love to be discontinued because of a bad average rating! I've used the old Dirt since 2010, it was my go-to product. I was very upset when it became unavailable for over a year, I thought it had been discontinued but I was relieved when I found out it was going through a redesign and coming back. This new Dirt is different, that's true, but the aim is to make it more sustainable, which is a very good reason for a redesign! The packaging is beautiful (I love that it uses glass now instead of plastic), and the materials are vegan and environmentally-friendly. True, because of this it's a bit harder to emulsify, but in my opinion it does just as good of a job once you manage to get it emulsified (it just takes a bit more rubbing then before). It's the same level of hold as before (which was never very strong originally, as it is just a texturizing paste), and the smell is wonderful, one of my favorite things about it.
I'm not afraid to recommend it! If you've never tried the old version, don't be swayed by these negative reviews, they're biased!

text:
INSTRUCTION FOR THOSE WITH FINE HAIR. I have a full head of fine hair that needs product in order to look good. Keep that in mind, since products have different results depending on your hair type and amount. After testing out this Atlas Putty several different ways I’ve found that it has some great benefits if you use it along with other products as well.
I would not call it “thickening”. It does add some body and a little shine. And the unexpected surprise is that it also brought out the wave in my hair (most clays and other products I use tend to make my hair straighter).. It has what I would call a “soft hold” - easy to run my hands through band a feeling that there really isn’t any product in it at all. Yet it does keep my hair from being flat, which is its natural state without product.
The magic formula I have settled on is: After showering and shampooing, start with a thickening spray of some sort, like a sea salt spray with some added hold (some have it and some don’t). Once you’ve dried your hair then either go straight to the Atlas Putty, or use a little clay first and then go to the Atlas Putty. And go light with the Atlas. You can always add a little more, because it is quite soft out of the tin, and works into the hair quite easily. Sounds like a lot, but it takes me five to ten minutes to dry and style with all of these steps. And the results are really worth it. Whereas normally my hair is pretty limp, using these steps results in tons of compliments. Oh and yes, the smell is nice. An added plus.
I don’t think this will be a product I use every day, but it will definitely be in my rotation (OK - I’m a bit of a product hoarder). Worth the money and a great product overall.

Cheaper than their awesome individual components. First off, the individual products are awesome. I'll address those in a minute. Let's price the items individually:

[[ASIN:B00023575I Anthony Logistics for Men Shave Cream, 6 Ounce]] is $15.91 at the time of this review.
[[ASIN:B000HPBR9G Anthony Logistics for Men Pre Shave Oil, 2 Ounce]] is $18.99 at the time of this review.
[[ASIN:B000VJVA0Y Anthony After Shave Balm]] is $15.97 at the time of this review.
and [[ASIN:B0001XDU2Q Anthony Logistics For Men Glycolic Cleanser, 8-Ounce]] is $17.99 at the time of this review.

That's $68.86 individually without the bag. This is actually preferable when I need refills these items.

The glycolic cleanser actually doesn't lather but leaves a pretty clean face for shaving. I used about a quarter size drop and wash my face before the shave.

The shave cream is superb. It doesn't require much at all. Just add a touch of warm water or the water on your face if you're in the shower and rub, rub, rub. I use my hand but you could use one of those fancy brushes like they did at the shave-and-a-hair-cut-two-bits barber shops your grandpappy used to go to. It will lather up and the 6 oz container lasts me for about 2-3 months at 7 shaves a week.

The after shave balm is like the cherry on your sundae. It's very refreshing and smells and feels awesome. If I had to pick one item only, I'd use this after any shave, period.

I don't use the pre-shave oil mainly because I never let my growth get long enough to use. The recommended usage is for men who have a short beard going and need to condition it for removal. Usually not me.

text:
Great product! A nice boost to your moisturizing routine. I received Dr. Au's face oil serum about 2 weeks ago and have been using it about every other day since I got it. Although it's a small bottle, you can tell by the look and feel of the serum that it is high quality and you really only need a few drops with each application. Since I started using it, there is a noticeable difference in my skin tone and it looks a lot more even. I have a lot of acne scars and they are already starting to fade significantly even though I don't apply the serum every day. I was worried that since it's an oil-based serum, I thought it would leave my face way too oily and thought it might make me break out more, but it really doesn't make you feel like you just slathered oil on your face. I have less breakouts, too.

The first few times I used it, I used about 7 drops to cover my entire face and neck (although you could probably use a little less). Although it's not extremely oily, it still leaves your face feeling like there's still a little something on it, so I started adding a few drops (maybe 4) in with my regular moisturizer and I'm in love, no oily residue in sight.
The oil itself is a little shimmery and needs to be shaken up a bit between each use. It comes with a little dropper built-in to the cap so you can add as little or as much as you want. It has a faint smell of vanilla, but it's just a touch, not overpowering at all. I can't smell it after application.

Overall, great product! Definitely will buy again and would recommend to add into your moisturizing routine. Would probably be good with an overnight face mask, too, although I haven't tried it yet. I couldn't give 5 stars because I really haven't been using the product long enough to see the full results. Perhaps I'll update my review after using the product more.

Scent: As someone switching from beard oils with fairly strong scents, I initially thought this balm was scentless. I think this can be a positive or a negative depending on your preferences. Strength: The hold is great! My beard is about an inch and a half to two inches, and this has provided the perfect amount of hold for me. It helps me to be able to do a little bit of shaping when I need to, but mostly allows my beard to be itself. It has also left my beard feeling less dry and looking a little bit healthier.

A return option is available, but returning near-empty bottles in a soaked cardboard box just seems silly. Pretty disappointed at the moment.

Does what it claims.. So, I've been using this brush for a good 5 months. The brush does what it claims to be able to do. The thing is, it's horse hair. This means that they will be softer than boar bristles. It's very good, and effective for short beards, or soft hair; I have VERY coarse hair. It's awesome for the mustache! Pros:
A good distributor of beard oil.
Hairs do stay in the brush, I've had a few come out over 5 months. (8 hairs to be exact).
Very handy and portable.
A good bang for the buck.

Cons:
Not suitable for guys with long beards, even if they have soft and fine hair.
Not suitable for coarse hair.
Due to real hair, may develop a pungent smell, if used on wet hair.
Not very easy to clean.
Can't be a double purpose brush that can work with hair on head, along with facial hair.

text:
Awesome value and great selection of scents!. With (6) one ounce jars to sample from the value here is really amazing considering you get six different scents to try.

It’s hard to pull the trigger on a single full-size jar just based on the descriptions of what the ingredients are so a sampler is very appreciated.

The 1 ounce jars will actually last quite a while if you’re using the proper amount of beard butter, which isn’t very much per application, so it’s not like these are one or two use jars either.

When you go by the scent profiles alone it’s hard to pull the trigger on a full size jar if you’re not quite sure what it’s gonna smell like in your beard. Just based off the scent profiles I would’ve ordered jars that I wasn’t 100% pleased after receiving them with but the sampler took away that risk.

For instance based on the scent profile I never would have ordered the “Corktown” scent because one of the scents in that profile is tobacco and that doesn’t seem like something I would like but Corktown is by far my favorite of the entire set and I will be ordering a full size jar straight away.

Detroit grooming is top quality stuff and the sampler is a very affordable way to take the guesswork out of what you should be buying next in full size.

The only negative I would give this sampler is there is no scent profile included on the jars or on the box so in order to find out what each scent profile is you either need to go to their website or look up the full size jars on Amazon and look at the pictures as the full size jars have the scent profile on the label. Not a big deal as it just takes a minute or two but if the scent profiles were included with the sampler that would save you a step.

text:
Not what I ordered - buyer beware.. I had purchased this previously. Despite people complaining about the pumice/lava rock, I rather liked the soap bar and the smell. So much so, that when I ran out I came right back to my order history and ordered it again. Much to my dismay the product that came was different. Gone were the exfoliating bits, and the scent, and now there was an offensive patchouli and citrus smell. text:
Snozzle with Xtava Black Orchid and Conair Infinity Pro. Similar to some of the other reviewers experiences, I find that the SnozzlePro works pretty well for me, but I do have to be very careful and make frequent adjustments -- it sort of exploits design problems with the tools you are using. I used it with a Conair Infinity ProPro and an Xtava Black Orchid.

Pros:
-It definitely fits my Conair Infinity Pro and probably won't have any trouble fitting other hair dryers.
-It's thick enough to be sturdy, but thin enough that I can stretch it onto the hair dryer.
- I don't experience any leaking or weird smells.
-I can use it (carefully) with the Xtava.

Cons:
-It is made of rubber, so when it heats up the rubber becomes more pliable and loose around the diffuser. I would recommend using this with cold air if possible. Unfortunately, my Conair Infinity Pro has a setting for "Cool" that isn't cold enough. So, I find that this works best if I keep my finger on the blue "Cold Shot" button the whole time.
-The Xtava has a very short connection point, so even though the SnozzlePro works pretty well, there's not a ton of space for it to hold on. That's a problem with the Xtava though, not the SnozzlePro. In particular, it seems to detach most at the top of the connection point and it will fall off while I'm using it. I just sort of use it gently and keep an eye on that top part to make sure it isn't slipping out.

Overall, I think the SnozzlePro is a great product that would probably work best with a diffuser with a longer connection point than the Xtava and potentially a hair dryer that has a truly cold setting.
